source.original_text: Chewi arXiv:2605.07006v1 Exercise3.3. Let f(x)=inner(x,A*x)/2 for a positive-definite symmetric matrix A on Euclidean space. Derive the gradient-descent iterates explicitly and check how sharp the results of this section are. The actual update is x_(n+1)=x_n-h gradient f(x_n). The exercise prints no solution. ASTIS-authored faithful paraphrase. The operator-power and eigenmode identities are selected proof components; full assessment of every Section3 rate remains an uncovered source obligation.

blind_reconstruction.text: For every complete real inner product space E, every continuous real-linear endomorphism H:E→E satisfying ⟨Hu,v⟩=⟨u,Hv⟩ for all u,v∈E, every μ∈ℝ and every x∈E with Hx=μx, define f(y)=⟨y,Hy⟩/2. For every h∈ℝ and N∈ℕ, put z=T^[N](x), where T(y)=y−h∇f(y). Then simultaneously z=(1−hμ)^N x, ‖z‖=|1−hμ|^N‖x‖, and f(z)=(1−hμ)^(2N)f(x). Here iteration at N=0 is the identity and every zeroth power, including 0^0, is 1. Neither x≠0 nor μ>0 nor h>0 is assumed, and there is no step-size restriction. Thus zero starting vectors, zero step size, zero μ, and 1−hμ=0 are included. In the last case z=0 for N≥1, whereas N=0 still gives z=x. These are exact identities and assert no contraction, decay rate, convergence, or sign of f.

import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Mul
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Calculus
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Symmetric
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Eigenspace.Basic

/-!
# Exact gradient descent on a quadratic objective

Chewi arXiv:2605.07006v1 Exercise3.3. Symmetry gives the actual gradient of
`f(x)=⟪x,Hx⟫/2`; the iteration is then a power of `I-hH`. A supplied eigenmode
has an exact trajectory, norm and objective value. The symmetric Hilbert and
arbitrary-step identities extend the positive-definite Euclidean source; they
do not assert spectral endpoint existence or convergence for every step.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.QuadraticGradientDescent

open InnerProductSpace
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- Actual quadratic-gradient iterates equal the powers of the linear update. -/
theorem quadratic_gradient_iterate (H : E →L[ℝ] E) (hH : H.IsSymmetric)
    (h : ℝ) (N : ℕ) (x : E) :
    let f := fun z : E => inner ℝ z (H z) / 2
    (fun z => z - h • gradient f z)^[N] x = ((1 - h • H) ^ N) x := by
  let f := fun z : E => inner ℝ z (H z) / 2
  have hg (z : E) : gradient f z = H z := by
    have hraw := ((hasFDerivAt_id z).inner ℝ H.hasFDerivAt).const_mul (1 / 2 : ℝ)
    have hlin : (1 / 2 : ℝ) •
        ((fderivInnerCLM ℝ (z, H z)).comp ((ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ E).prod H)) =
        toDual ℝ E (H z) := by
      ext v
      change (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (inner ℝ z (H v) + inner ℝ v (H z)) = inner ℝ (H z) v
      rw [← hH.apply_clm z v, (real_inner_comm v (H z)).symm]
      ring
    have hd : HasFDerivAt f (toDual ℝ E (H z)) z := by
      convert hraw using 1 <;> first | rfl | exact hlin.symm | (ext v; simp only [f, id_eq]; ring)
    exact (hasGradientAt_iff_hasFDerivAt.mpr hd).gradient
  change (fun z => z - h • gradient f z)^[N] x = _
  simp_rw [hg]
  exact congrFun (FunLike.coe_pow_eq_iterate (1 - h • H) N).symm x

/-- A supplied eigenmode gives exact iterates, distances to zero and quadratic values.
No existence of an eigenvector or stability of the chosen step is assumed. -/
theorem quadratic_eigenmode (H : E →L[ℝ] E) (hH : H.IsSymmetric)
    {μ : ℝ} {x : E} (hx : H x = μ • x) (h : ℝ) (N : ℕ) :
    let f := fun z : E => inner ℝ z (H z) / 2
    let z := (fun y => y - h • gradient f y)^[N] x
    z = (1 - h * μ) ^ N • x ∧
      ‖z‖ = |1 - h * μ| ^ N * ‖x‖ ∧
      f z = (1 - h * μ) ^ (2 * N) * f x := by
  let f := fun z : E => inner ℝ z (H z) / 2
  let A : E →L[ℝ] E := 1 - h • H
  have hAx : A x = (1 - h * μ) • x := by
    simp only [A, sub_apply, one_apply_eq_self,
      smul_apply, hx, smul_smul, sub_smul, one_smul]
  have hp : (A ^ N) x = (1 - h * μ) ^ N • x := by
    by_cases hz : x = 0
    · simp [hz]
    · have he : Module.End.HasEigenvector A.toLinearMap (1 - h * μ) x :=
        ⟨Module.End.mem_eigenspace_iff.mpr hAx, hz⟩
      have ht := congrArg (fun K : E →ₗ[ℝ] E => K x) (ContinuousLinearMap.toLinearMap_pow A N)
      convert ht.trans (he.pow_apply N) using 1; rfl
  have hi := (quadratic_gradient_iterate H hH h N x).trans hp
  change _ = _ ∧ _ = _ ∧ f _ = _ * f x
  rw [hi]
  refine ⟨rfl, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs]
  · simp only [f, map_smul, inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right, RCLike.conj_to_real]
    rw [Nat.mul_comm 2 N, pow_mul]
    ring

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.QuadraticGradientDescent

lesson.title: Exact evolution of a quadratic eigenmode
lesson.statement: The supplied eigenmode evolves by a scalar geometric factor, with the displayed exact norm and objective-value identities.
assumptions: E is a complete real inner-product space. H:E→E is a continuous linear operator symmetric in the sense ⟨Hx,y⟩=⟨x,Hy⟩ for every x,y.
Define the actual centered objective f(x)=⟨x,Hx⟩/2 and its actual gradient update T_h(x)=x−h∇f(x). h∈ℝ is constant across steps, N∈ℕ, and the initial point x∈E is arbitrary.
μ∈ℝ and Hx=μx is supplied for the initial point. x=0 is allowed as an algebraic mode relation; a genuine eigenvector requires x≠0.

steps.title: Transport the supplied mode to the update operator
steps.text: The given relation Hx=μx implies (I−hH)x=(1−hμ)x. If x=0, every power identity is immediate. Otherwise this is a genuine nonzero eigenvector of I−hH, so Mathlib’s eigenvector power theorem applies. No eigenvector is constructed.

steps.title: Read the exact norm and value
steps.text: Take norms of the scalar multiple and use homogeneity. The quadratic is homogeneous of degree two, so its value is multiplied by the square of the trajectory scalar. The absolute value is essential when the update changes sign.
